findings.tool_name: OpenAI models (GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini) via Azure
findings.finding: DOL gave staff access to two OpenAI models through Microsoft Azure in April 2025, on an internal platform offering applications like a translator, pros/cons analyzer, and memo writer.
findings.exact_quote: The two OpenAI models now available to Labor staff are GPT-4o and GPT-4o mini
findings.source_title: OpenAI tech is now available at the Labor Department, FedScoop
findings.notes: VERIFIED against full page: FedScoop carries 'The two OpenAI models now available to Labor staff are GPT-4o and GPT-4o mini' verbatim. The FedScoop article confirms Labor 'staff' can access the OpenAI models but gives no seat count and does not say all ~15,000 DOL employees have access. The deployment is real but framed around specific guided applications (translator, memo writer) on an internal platform rather than an unrestricted enterprise chat rollout. This corroborates and slightly extends the inventory's in-house 'Generative AI Assistant (AI Center)' entry: the underlying engine is OpenAI's GPT-4o family. No public source quantifies coverage; treat as a deliberate rollout of unknown breadth.

findings.finding: No DOL-specific public statement found confirming a department-wide Microsoft Copilot Chat rollout or seat count.
findings.notes: Searched FedScoop, Nextgov, GovExec and dol.gov for a DOL Copilot rollout announcement and seat figures; none found. DOL is plausibly covered by the Sept 2025 GSA-Microsoft OneGov deal (free M365 Copilot Chat for G5 customers government-wide) but no DOL-specific confirmation exists. The dol.gov AI strategy PDF returned HTTP 403 and could not be fetched. Recording honestly as no DOL-specific source.

findings.finding: NRC launched SimplifAI, an OpenAI-powered internal chatbot accessed via an internal website, in August 2025 as a productivity tool available to staff on an opt-in basis.
findings.exact_quote: The tool is powered by an OpenAI model and launched in August 2025.
findings.source_title: NRC uses more AI than its inventory suggests, FedScoop
findings.notes: VERIFIED against full page: FedScoop carries 'The tool is powered by an OpenAI model and launched in August 2025.' verbatim. SimplifAI corresponds to the inventory's 'Unified, secure access to multiple advanced AI language models' / 'Text Retrieval and Generation for NRC Staff Support' entries. FedScoop confirms it works like commercial chat ('an employee goes to an internal website, enters a query and gets a response') and answers from NRC documents. Adoption is explicitly voluntary: 'This isn't something that we are forcing on anyone.' No seat count or agency-wide claim is public; against a ~3,000-person workforce coverage is unquantified. This is a deliberate rollout, not just technical availability.

findings.finding: NSF's documented Copilot use is a limited pilot confined to its Directorate for Technology, Innovation and Partnerships (TIP), not an agency-wide deployment.
findings.source_title: Artificial Intelligence Policy and Strategy - Policies, NSF
findings.notes: The inventory itself labels this the 'TIP MS Copilot Pilot.' Public searches found no NSF-specific seat count, no statement of all ~1,700 employees having access, and no NSF-named participation in the GSA OneGov ChatGPT/Copilot deals. NSF's other AI entry ('Open access LLM') is described as open-source models (Llama, BART, etc.) for document summarization run inside the firewall - a task-specific tool, not a general-purpose chat assistant. Coverage is genuinely pilot-stage and narrow; recorded honestly. Could not extract a verbatim scale quote from nsf.gov/policies/ai.

findings.tool_name: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and OpenAI ChatGPT (GPT-5)
findings.finding: OPM rolled out Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and ChatGPT-5 to its entire workforce in September 2025 under the GSA OneGov deals, with the director stating the goal that everyone have it.
findings.exact_quote: My goal is everybody should have it on their laptops, everybody should do the free trainings that are online and everybody should just play with it.
findings.source_title: OPM adds OpenAI to its employees' computers, Nextgov/FCW
findings.notes: VERIFIED against full page: Nextgov carries the OPM director's quote 'My goal is everybody should have it on their laptops, everybody should do the free trainings that are online and everybody should just play with it.' verbatim. Strongly corroborated. FedScoop separately reports Director Scott Kupor told staff M365 Copilot Chat 'became available Monday' and ChatGPT-5 would be available 'over the next few days' to all workers. This is a genuine agency-wide deliberate rollout, not mere technical availability. The Nextgov quote is the director's stated intent for universal coverage; combined with the FedScoop 'all workers' language, coverage is assessed 'all' against the ~6,000 workforce. Note the inventory lists Anthropic Claude as used across OPM; press reporting indicates OPM later halted agency-wide Claude use - the Copilot/ChatGPT rollout supersedes it as the current general-purpose offering.

findings.finding: The inventory lists Claude as used across OPM for summarization, drafting and decision support, but press reporting indicates OPM subsequently halted agency-wide Claude use.
findings.source_title: NASA chatbots, Treasury coding, OPM drafting: How agencies have deployed Claude, FedScoop
findings.notes: The OMB inventory field describes Claude as 'LLM used across OPM,' but searches surfaced reporting that OPM halted its previously disclosed Claude use. Could not fetch a verbatim quote confirming the halt or any Claude seat count, so recorded with low confidence. The current general-purpose offering at OPM is the Copilot/ChatGPT rollout above; this finding flags a likely discrepancy between the static inventory field and the evolved reality.

findings.finding: The OMB inventory reports 5,001-10,000 SBA users for these tools, but GAO and FedScoop reporting indicate SBA paused essentially all AI use in March 2025, contradicting an active broad deployment.
findings.estimated_users: inventory says 5,001-10,000; likely overstated given the AI pause
findings.exact_quote: The pause was intended to give the agency time to review use case compliance with new executive orders
findings.source_title: SBA behind the eightball on AI use case reporting, GAO finds, FedScoop
findings.notes: VERIFIED against full page: FedScoop carries 'The pause was intended to give the agency time to review use case compliance with new executive orders' verbatim (full sentence continues '...and to reflect any change in priorities from the SBA's new chief information and chief AI officers.'). Sharp discrepancy with the inventory field. FedScoop (citing GAO) reports SBA stated as of March 2025 that all 21 of its 2024 use cases were 'either decommissioned, never deployed, or paused,' and that as of April 2026 the pause remained in effect except for seven pilot/pre-pilot projects in fraud detection, IT ops and cybersecurity - none of which are general-purpose chat assistants. The inventory's 5,001-10,000 figure for Copilot/Perplexity/Gemini/Grammarly likely reflects pre-pause licensing breadth (the SBA workforce balloons with disaster staff) rather than an actively rolled-out, currently-available general-purpose AI tool. Treat the seat count as a licensing-availability number, not confirmed active deployment.

findings.finding: SSA began rolling out the Agency Support Companion, an OpenAI-powered internal generative AI chatbot for employees, announced via internal email in April 2025; staff must complete a four-minute training video to access it.
findings.exact_quote: Staff have to watch a four-minute video with guidelines and best practices to access it.
findings.source_title: SSA is rolling out a new chatbot for employees, Nextgov/FCW
findings.notes: VERIFIED against full page: Nextgov carries 'Staff have to watch a four-minute video with guidelines and best practices to access it.' verbatim. Corroborates the inventory's 'Agency Support Companion (ASC)' entry. Nextgov confirms the tool uses an OpenAI model (GPT-4o mini per its linked source), was not trained on SSA data, is for content creation, summarization, research and coding assistance, and is not configured to learn from interactions. The rollout is a deliberate agency-wide offer to employees (announced to staff broadly via internal email), but no public source quantifies how many of SSA's ~60,000 (reported ~57,000) employees actually have or use access. The four-minute-video gate suggests opt-in adoption rather than automatic universal provisioning. Coverage unquantified.
